result.builder:
Criteria the build must meet (the expect lines, word for word):
- math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
- clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
- README.md documents every function math.js exports
- npm test passes

Steps:
1. Read math.js, README.md, test/math.test.js and package.json (tests run with `node --test`). math.js currently exports add, subtract and multiply via `module.exports = { ... }`.
2. In math.js add a function `clamp(x, lo, hi)` with a short doc comment in the existing style. If `lo > hi`, throw `new RangeError(...)` with a clear message. Otherwise return `lo` when `x < lo`, `hi` when `x > hi`, and `x` otherwise (so clamp(-5, 0, 100) is 0, clamp(140, 0, 100) is 100, clamp(50, 0, 100) is 50, and lo === hi returns that value). Add `clamp` to the `module.exports` object, keeping the existing exports.
3. In test/math.test.js import clamp and add tests: values below, above and inside the range, the boundaries themselves, lo === hi, and `assert.throws(() => clamp(1, 10, 0), RangeError)`.
4. In README.md's `## API` section, make sure every function math.js exports has its own `### name(args)` heading with a one-line description and a small example, matching the existing entries. Note that `subtract(a, b)` is exported but currently NOT documented in README.md — add an entry for it as well as one for `clamp(x, lo, hi)` (mention that it throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi). Keep the existing add and multiply entries.
5. Run `npm test` and make sure it exits 0 with no failing tests. Also run `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./math.js')))"` and confirm every listed name appears as a heading in README.md's API section.
6. Commit the changes to math.js, test/math.test.js and README.md and open one pull request that references https://github.com/o/r/issues/23.
result.verifier:
At the PR head, from the repository root, run each check in order. Each check corresponds to one expect line.

Check 1 — expect: "math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi"
Run:
node -e "const m=require('./math.js'); const c=m.clamp; if(typeof c!=='function') throw new Error('clamp not exported'); const cases=[[-5,0,100,0],[140,0,100,100],[50,0,100,50],[0,0,100,0],[100,0,100,100],[7,3,3,3],[-10,-20,-5,-10],[-30,-20,-5,-20],[2.5,0,1,1]]; for(const [x,lo,hi,e] of cases){const r=c(x,lo,hi); if(r!==e) throw new Error('clamp('+x+','+lo+','+hi+')='+r+' expected '+e);} console.log('OK')"
PASS: prints OK and exits 0. FAIL: clamp is missing or not a function, or any case returns a value other than the expected one (an error is thrown / non-zero exit).

Check 2 — expect: "clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi"
Run:
node -e "const {clamp}=require('./math.js'); for(const [x,lo,hi] of [[5,10,0],[0,1,0],[-3,-1,-2]]){let err=null; try{clamp(x,lo,hi)}catch(e){err=e} if(!(err instanceof RangeError)) throw new Error('clamp('+x+','+lo+','+hi+') did not throw RangeError: '+err);} console.log('OK')"
PASS: prints OK and exits 0. FAIL: any call returns normally or throws something that is not a RangeError.

Check 3 — expect: "README.md documents every function math.js exports"
Run:
node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const names=Object.keys(require('./math.js')).filter(k=>typeof require('./math.js')[k]==='function'); const md=fs.readFileSync('README.md','utf8'); const missing=names.filter(n=>!new RegExp('^#+\\s*'+n+'\\s*\\(','m').test(md)); console.log('exports:',names.join(',')); if(missing.length) throw new Error('undocumented: '+missing.join(',')); console.log('OK')"
Then open README.md and confirm each exported function's entry actually describes what that function does.
PASS: the script prints OK (every exported function — expected to include add, subtract, multiply and clamp — has a heading in README.md) and each such entry describes the function. FAIL: any exported function has no README.md entry (note subtract was undocumented before this change), or an entry is only a bare name with no description.

Check 4 — expect: "npm test passes"
Run: npm test ; echo EXIT=$?
PASS: EXIT=0 and the output reports `# fail 0`. FAIL: non-zero exit or any failing test.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Check that test/math.test.js gained tests for clamp, including the RangeError case.
- Check that the README clamp entry mentions the RangeError for lo greater than hi.
- Note the behaviour of clamp with NaN inputs, if any, as an observation only.
